# Fatou Lemma

In mathematics, the **Fatou lemma** establishes an inequality relating the
Lebesgue integral of the limit inferior of a sequence of functions to the limit
inferior of integrals of these functions.

:::{.theorem data-title="Fatou's Lemma"}

If $X_{n}\geq 0$ then
$$
\liminf_{n \to \infty}\mathbb{E}[X_{n}] \geq  \mathbb{E}\left[\liminf_{n \to \infty}X_{n}\right].
$$

:::

*Proof:*
Define
$$
Y_k(\omega) := \inf_{n\ge k} X_n(\omega), \qquad k \ge 1.
$$
Then each $Y_k$ is measurable and nonnegative, and
$$
Y_k \uparrow \liminf_{n\to\infty} X_n \quad \text{pointwise as } k\to\infty.
$$
By the [Monotone Convergence Theorem](Monotone%20Convergence%20Theorem.md),
$$
\mathbb E\!\left[\liminf_{n\to\infty} X_n\right]
= \mathbb E\!\left[\lim_{k\to\infty} Y_k\right]
= \lim_{k\to\infty} \mathbb E[Y_k].
$$
For each $k$, since $Y_k \le X_n$ for all $n \ge k$,
$$
\mathbb E[Y_k] \le \inf_{n\ge k} \mathbb E[X_n].
$$
Taking limits in $k$,
$$
\lim_{k\to\infty} \mathbb E[Y_k]
\le \lim_{k\to\infty} \inf_{n\ge k} \mathbb E[X_n]
= \liminf_{n\to\infty} \mathbb E[X_n].
$$
This proves the result.
$\square$
